# Thermovance TVC-Series High-Density Cold Plates & Application Note TAN-08

# Thermovance TVC-Series Brazed Fin Cold Plates
## Catalogue Data & Engineering Application Note TAN-08

### 1. Catalogue Specifications (Dual-Module Footprint Envelope)
All TVC-Series cold plates feature internal corrugated lanced-offset fin cores designed to accommodate two power modules mounted in tandem along the flow axis (**Flow Topology S: Series-Serpentine**).

| Model | Alloy | Parallel Channels $N_{\text{ch}}$ | Channel Area $A_{\text{ch}}$ ($	ext{mm}^2$) | Active Fin Width $W_f$ (mm) | Water Thermal Resistance $R_{\text{th,cat}}$ (K/W per module) | Core Hydraulic Factor $K_{\text{hyd}}$ | Port Loss Factor $K_{\text{port}}$ | Mass (kg) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **TVC-180-AL** | Al 6061-T6 | 14 | 3.00 | 90.0 | 0.0500 | 1.240 | 0.115 | 1.15 |
| **TVC-200-AL** | Al 6061-T6 | 18 | 3.00 | 90.0 | 0.0485 | 0.980 | 0.098 | 1.45 |
| **TVC-250-AL** | Al 6061-T6 | 16 | 4.00 | 75.0 | 0.0451 | 1.070 | 0.100 | 1.85 |
| **TVC-220-CU** | Cu C11000 | 16 | 3.00 | 75.0 | 0.0395 | 1.200 | 0.110 | 2.60 |
| **TVC-260-CU** | Cu C11000 | 20 | 3.00 | 75.0 | 0.0380 | 0.940 | 0.095 | 3.10 |

**Maximum Permissible Channel Velocity ($v_{\max}$) for Erosion-Corrosion Prevention:**
- **Aluminum 6061-T6 (-AL models):** $v_{\max} = 2.20\text{ m/s}$
- **Copper C11000 (-CU models):** $v_{\max} = 3.50\text{ m/s}$

Channel velocity is calculated from total volumetric flow rate $Q_v$ ($\text{m}^3/\text{s}$):
$$v_{\text{ch}} = \frac{Q_v}{N_{\text{ch}} \cdot A_{\text{ch}}}$$

---

### 2. Hydraulic Pressure Drop with Glycol Coolants
Catalogue resistance coefficients $K_{\text{hyd}}$ are calibrated using pure deionized water at $25\text{ }^\circ\text{C}$ ($\rho_{\text{ref}} = 997\text{ kg/m}^3$, $\nu_{\text{ref}} = 0.890 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2/\text{s}$). When operating with aqueous glycol solutions at volumetric flow rate $Q_{\text{Lpm}}$ (in $\text{L/min}$), the total assembly pressure drop $\Delta P_{\text{total}}$ (in kPa) is the sum of the viscosity-corrected fin-core drop and the turbulent manifold port loss:
$$\Delta P_{\text{core}} = K_{\text{hyd}} \left(\frac{\rho}{\rho_{\text{ref}}}\right) \left(\frac{\nu}{\nu_{\text{ref}}}\right)^{0.25} Q_{\text{Lpm}}^{1.75}$$
$$\Delta P_{\text{port}} = K_{\text{port}} \left(\frac{\rho}{1000}\right) Q_{\text{Lpm}}^2$$
$$\Delta P_{\text{total}} = \Delta P_{\text{core}} + \Delta P_{\text{port}}$$
where $\rho$ is the coolant density ($\text{kg/m}^3$) and $\nu = \mu / \rho$ is the coolant kinematic viscosity ($\text{m}^2/\text{s}$).

---

### 3. Thermal Modeling & Derating Rules

#### 3.1 Series-Serpentine Coolant Temperature Reference
In all TVC-Series plates, the coolant flows sequentially beneath Module 1 (upstream) and Module 2 (downstream). Because internal fin conduction mixes the thermal boundary layer toward the exit of each zone, the peak baseplate temperature occurs at the trailing edge of **Module 2** and must be referenced to the **coolant outlet temperature** $T_{\text{out}}$:
$$T_{\text{out}} = T_{\text{in}} + \frac{P_{\text{total}}}{\dot{m} \cdot c_p}$$

#### 3.2 Glycol Convective & Lateral Footprint Constriction Multipliers
Catalogue thermal resistance $R_{\text{th,cat}}$ (at $Q_{\text{Lpm}} = 6.00\text{ L/min}$) is measured with pure water and a full-width heat source ($W_{\text{mod}} = W_f$). For actual applications, the effective cold-plate convective thermal resistance per module, $R_{\text{conv}}$, is:
$$R_{\text{conv}} = R_{\text{th,cat}} \cdot M_s \cdot F_{\text{gly}}$$
1. **Lateral Footprint Constriction Factor ($M_s$):** When the heat source width $W_{\text{mod}}$ (transverse to flow) is smaller than the active fin width $W_f$, fin-efficiency drop across the unloaded lateral channels increases resistance by:
   $$M_s = \left(\frac{W_f}{W_{\text{mod}}}\right)^{0.35}$$
2. **Glycol Convective Factor ($F_{\text{gly}}$):**
   - Pure water: $F_{\text{gly}} = 1.00$
   - 30/70 Ethylene Glycol / Water: $F_{\text{gly}} = 1.14$
   - 50/50 Ethylene Glycol / Water: $F_{\text{gly}} = 1.28$

#### 3.3 Peak Module Baseplate Temperature ($T_{b,\max}$)
With a thermal interface material (TIM) of areal resistance $R''_{\text{tim}}$ ($\text{K}\cdot\text{cm}^2/\text{W}$) over module footprint area $A_{\text{mod}}$ ($\text{cm}^2$), the TIM resistance per module is $R_{\text{tim}} = R''_{\text{tim}} / A_{\text{mod}}$. The peak baseplate temperature (Module 2) is:
$$T_{b,\max} = T_{\text{out}} + P_{\text{mod}} \cdot (R_{\text{tim}} + R_{\text{conv}})$$

### 1. Inputs and coolant state
- Total heat: P_total = 2 × 650 W = 1300 W
- Volumetric flow: Q_v = 6.00 L/min = 1.000e-4 m³/s
- Density: ρ = 1055 kg/m³; cp = 3450 J/(kg·K); μ = 0.00210 Pa·s
- Mass flow: m_dot = ρQ_v = 0.1055 kg/s
- Coolant rise: ΔT = P_total/(m_dot cp) = 1300/(0.1055×3450) = 3.572 K
- Outlet temperature: T_out = 45.0 + 3.572 = 48.572 °C
- Kinematic viscosity: ν = μ/ρ = 1.9905e-6 m²/s; ν_ref = 0.890e-6 m²/s
- Viscosity correction: (ν/ν_ref)^0.25 = (2.2365)^0.25 = 1.223
- Density correction: ρ/ρ_ref = 1055/997 = 1.0582
- Flow factor: Q_Lpm^1.75 = 6.00^1.75 = 23.00
- Core pressure multiplier: 1.0582 × 1.223 × 23.00 = 29.76 kPa per unit K_hyd
- Port pressure multiplier: (ρ/1000) Q^2 = 1.055 × 36.00 = 37.98 kPa per unit K_port
- TIM resistance: R_tim = 0.120 K·cm²/W / 36 cm² = 0.003333 K/W per module
- Heat-source transverse width: W_mod = 60 mm (60 mm footprint side transverse to flow)

### 2. Screening equations
- Channel velocity: v_ch = Q_v/(N_ch A_ch)
- Corrected pressure drop: ΔP_total = K_hyd(29.76) + K_port(37.98)
- Constriction factor: Ms = (W_f/60 mm)^0.35
- Glycol factor: F_gly = 1.28 for 50/50 EG/water
- Convective resistance: R_conv = R_th,cat Ms F_gly

Assumptions and basis:
- Static axial tension N = 90 kN = 90,000 N.
- Bar length L = 1.5 m; steel density = 7850 kg/m3.
- The 18 mm pin requires a hole. The hole diameter is taken as 18 mm (line-to-line) because no clearance or fit is specified. The net section through the hole governs the tensile stress. A 20 mm hole would give 150.0 MPa for the selected bar, still <= 155 MPa, so the selection is unchanged.
- Mass is the mass of the 1.5 m bar alone; the small mass removed by the hole is neglected.
- Catalogue: T4-56-1.md, Calder Sections Plainflat series. The catalogue states gross section area = width x thickness.

Calculation:
Required net area for 155 MPa: A_net,req = 90,000 / 155 = 580.65 mm2.
For each bar: A_net = (width - 18) x thickness; sigma_net = 90,000 / A_net; mass = A_g x 10^-6 x 7850 x 1.5.

Candidate check:

| PF-60x10 | 60 | 10 | 600 | 420 | 214.3 | 7.07 | fail net stress |
| PF-70x10 | 70 | 10 | 700 | 520 | 173.1 | 8.24 | fail net stress |
| PF-80x10 | 80 | 10 | 800 | 620 | 145.2 | 9.42 | pass; lightest compliant |
| PF-80x12 | 80 | 12 | 960 | 744 | 121.0 | 11.30 | pass; heavier |

All four bars satisfy width >= 40 mm, thickness >= 6 mm, and mass <= 20 kg. The controlling constraint is net-section tensile stress. PF-60x10 and PF-70x10 exceed 155 MPa at the net section. PF-80x10 is the lightest bar that passes:
- Net-section stress: 90,000 / 620 = 145.16 MPa, reported as 145.2 MPa <= 155 MPa.
- Gross stress away from the hole: 90,000 / 800 = 112.5 MPa.
- Mass: 800 x 10^-6 x 1.5 x 7850 = 9.42 kg <= 20 kg.
- Width: 80 mm >= 40 mm.
- Thickness: 10 mm >= 6 mm.

If the 155 MPa limit were applied only to gross-section average stress, PF-60x10 would be lighter (150.0 MPa gross, 7.07 kg), but it exceeds 155 MPa at the net section through the 18 mm pin hole (214.3 MPa). It is therefore not acceptable for this pin-connected tie. The selection PF-80x10 is based on the governing net-section tensile stress.

Note on proof of absence: the harness proof of absence for ask 1 concerns the external tension-member pages (Scribd, Lamar, Assakkaf, Purdue), which do not contain the Calder Plainflat catalogue. The catalogue is the reference document T4-56-1.md, and it does list the Plainflat models; therefore ask 1 is answered from T4-56-1.md and is not listed as not_stated.

Pin bearing, tear-out, and clevis details are outside the stated selection criteria. For information, the 80 mm width with a centred 18 mm hole leaves (80 - 18)/2 = 31 mm edge distance each side; this should be verified against the clevis and pin details in detailed design.

Effective Net Area in Tension Members
The document discusses tension members in steel structures. Key points include:
- Tension members resist axial tensile forces and come in various cross sectional shapes like rods, angles, and built-up sections.
- Net area is the cross sectional area minus reductions for holes, notches, etc. Effective net area further accounts for factors like shear lag that reduce a member's load carrying capacity.
- Design strength considers both yield strength based on gross area and block shear strength
